title: Anti-Recursion Protocol: Preventing Inward-Facing Gravity
purpose: Prevents the pattern where teams spend their time building coordination infrastructure to build more coordination infrastructure. Enforces a minimum ratio of domain work to infrastructure work. Based on the critical finding that Teams 22-28 (7 consecutive teams) all focused inward.
evidence_base: TT-3 finding: 'The repository is becoming a coordination system that coordinates the building of more coordination systems.'

section_1_domain_work_ratio.title: Mandatory Domain Work Ratio
section_1_domain_work_ratio.description: Every operation must allocate a minimum percentage of agent capacity to domain work (market research, data analysis, tool building for external use).

rules.rule: Minimum 60% of agent capacity on domain work
rules.definition: Domain work = any work that produces artifacts used OUTSIDE the coordination system. Examples: market research picks, data analysis reports, external API tools, knowledge base entries about domain topics (not coordination topics).
rules.measurement: Count agents. At least 60% must be assigned domain tasks.
rules.exception: New session after a system failure — may spend up to 100% on recovery for one session only

rules.rule: Maximum 30% of agent capacity on infrastructure
rules.definition: Infrastructure work = modifications to coordination system, SOPs, bus, protocols, monitoring tools, dashboards.
rules.hard_cap: No more than 3 infrastructure agents in any single operation regardless of team size

rules.definition: KB entries, session logs, index updates. This is overhead, not discretionary.

enforcement.pre_launch_check: Before launching, coordinator tallies agents by category. If domain < 60% or infra > 30%, must rebalance.
enforcement.mid_session_check: At CP-3 (mid-session), verify domain agents are actually doing domain work (not drifting into infra)
enforcement.post_session_audit: Session log must report actual domain/infra/overhead split with evidence

section_2_infrastructure_freeze.title: Infrastructure Modification Controls
section_2_infrastructure_freeze.description: The coordination system is mature enough for production use. Further changes require justification.

freeze_rules.rule: No new SOPs unless a genuinely novel failure mode is encountered
freeze_rules.test: Can you point to a specific incident where the existing 13 SOPs were insufficient? If no → do not create a new SOP.
freeze_rules.rationale: 13 SOPs + 10 ASR rules approaches process overhead saturation per TT-3 analysis

freeze_rules.rule: No new coordination modules unless blocking a domain task
freeze_rules.test: Is a domain team unable to complete their work due to a missing coordination feature? If no → do not build it.
freeze_rules.rationale: Teams 22-28 built 5 new coordination modules (help protocol, work stealing, direct channels, coordinator hub, SDK launcher) without any domain team requesting them

freeze_rules.rule: Bug fixes to existing infrastructure are always allowed
freeze_rules.rationale: The 2 high-severity bugs (fulfill_help transaction, complete_work TOCTOU) and 15 medium-severity bugs should be fixed. Fixing != building new.

freeze_rules.rule: Performance improvements to existing infrastructure require evidence of bottleneck
freeze_rules.test: Can you show monitoring data where infrastructure performance blocked domain work? If no → do not optimize.

section_3_recursion_detection.title: Detecting Recursive Patterns
section_3_recursion_detection.description: Signs that the team is falling into inward-facing gravity.

warning_signs.sign: Think tanks analyzing the coordination system
warning_signs.action: Redirect to domain analysis. The coordination system does not need more analysis.

warning_signs.detection: Output path is in storage/coordination/ and not a bug fix
warning_signs.action: Verify this was explicitly requested to unblock a domain task. If not, redirect.

warning_signs.detection: Research questions about agent communication, coordination, or orchestration
warning_signs.action: Unless this is academic research for KB, redirect to domain research (market analysis, API evaluation, etc.)

warning_signs.sign: Session log has zero domain artifacts
warning_signs.detection: No market picks, no domain KB entries, no external-facing tools produced
warning_signs.action: Flag as AR violation. Next session MUST be domain-focused.
Apply FREEZE-01 test. Block unless novel failure mode documented.

section_4_domain_work_catalog.title: Approved Domain Work Categories
section_4_domain_work_catalog.description: Pre-approved domain work that teams should prioritize over infrastructure.

high_priority.action: Execute SOP-018. Use existing methods in market-research/methods/. Log picks.

high_priority.status: Tools built (13 scripts) but not used for systematic gathering since T14
high_priority.action: Run data gathering operations using existing tools. Populate storage/sources/.

high_priority.category: API Tool Building for External Data
high_priority.status: 5 tool gaps identified by TT-OBS-2: StackOverflow, PubMed, Reddit, PyPI/npm, CrossRef
high_priority.action: Build tools that enable domain research. These are domain-enabling, not infrastructure.

medium_priority.action: Create KB entries about domain topics: market analysis techniques, data sources evaluation, industry trends
Use gathered data to produce analytical reports. Apply methods from market-research/methods/.

pre_launch: Domain agent count ≥ 60% of total agents
Infrastructure agent count ≤ 30% of total (max 3 agents)
At least one domain deliverable defined in operation objectives
No new SOP creation planned (unless FREEZE-01 test passes)
No new coordination module planned (unless FREEZE-02 test passes)
post_session: Domain artifacts produced (picks, reports, tools, domain KB entries)
Actual domain/infra/overhead split recorded in session log
If zero domain output: document why and commit to domain-first next session
